feedback: If a learner writes 3/7 for the bag, recount the whole set aloud including the favourable outcomes: everything that could be drawn is 10, so 10 goes on the bottom, giving 3/10.

If a learner applies the formula to an uneven spinner, prompt the equally-likely check first: when sections are different sizes the colour counts are not counts of equally-likely outcomes, so the simple formula does not apply.

If a learner leaves 2/8 unsimplified or reduces it wrongly, scaffold the simplifying step and confirm 1/4 sits at the same point on the 0-to-1 scale \u2014 simplifying does not change the actual chance.
If a learner combines numbers arbitrarily with no favourable-over-total structure, return to counting favourable, then total, then writing the fraction.
activities.intendedInsight: The denominator is the whole set of equally-likely outcomes, favourable included \u2014 so P(blue) among 3 blue and 7 red is 3/10, not 3/7. The simple favourable/total formula only applies when outcomes are equally likely, and simplifying (2/8 = 1/4) names the same point on the 0-to-1 scale.
learnerActions: Work a short series of problems, each a probability to be formed and then simplified: (a) a bag of 3 blue and 7 red marbles \u2014 find P(blue); (b) a fair six-sided die \u2014 find P(rolling a 4); (c) a spinner with 8 equal sections, 2 of them gold \u2014 find P(gold).
For each item, first confirm the outcomes are equally likely, then count the favourable outcomes, then count the WHOLE set of possible outcomes (including the favourable ones) for the denominator.
Write each probability as a fraction and simplify where possible (e.g. 2/8 \u2192 1/4).
On the bag item, if you write 3/7, stop and recount: the denominator is all 10 marbles, including the 3 blue ones, so the answer is 3/10.
Encounter at least one unequal-outcome situation (e.g. an uneven spinner with different-sized sections) and decide whether the simple formula applies before using it.
activities.title: Varied probability ladder with simplest form

feedback: If a learner expects only the numerator to matter, vary the non-favourable counts and show that the denominator (whole set) and the scale marker both respond \u2014 e.g. adding red marbles enlarges the total, so P(blue) falls (as long as the bag has at least one blue; with no blue it stays 0).
Confirm that the simplified fraction lands on the same point of the 0-to-1 line as the unsimplified one \u2014 the chance is unchanged.
activities.intendedInsight: More favourable outcomes relative to the whole set raise the probability; the denominator is always the whole outcome set. Seeing the fraction and its position on the scale update as the bag changes connects composition to the value of the probability.
learnerActions: Edit the composition of a bag (e.g. add or remove blue and red counters) and read the probability fraction as it forms.
Identify the WHOLE set as the denominator each time the bag changes, confirming favourable counters are part of that total.
Watch the simplified form of the fraction and a marker on a 0-to-1 line move as the composition changes.
Predict: 'If I add 5 more red marbles, which number in the fraction changes, and does P(blue) go up or down?' then check against the live display.
activities.title: Editable bag: watch the fraction form and simplify
